inventory_note: Initial T1 syntax inventory; all findings are unaudited debt, not approved behavior. Lower counts as owning tracks repair them. New exceptions require a fixed reason and justification.

exceptions.justification: Walks an already materialized finite Python exception cause chain to classify SQLSTATE before retry; object identities are recorded in seen and repeated identities or None terminate traversal. It performs no external wait or sleep.

Bounded diagnostic normalization to the durable byte contract, not an external wait: each iteration removes an ancillary observation or halves a nontrivial text field. The finite item/text measure strictly decreases; when only structural/scalar fields remain it rejects an oversized document rather than repeating. Typed failure and exit facts remain explicit.

Pure finite decoding of one immutable RawValue object: each successful MapAccess next_entry consumes a complete key/value, closing brace ends iteration and malformed/EOF errors propagate. The owning original_value refuses depth >=128. This is not polling or an external wait; parse_strict has no universal byte ceiling and caller-specific HTTP/checkpoint byte budgets remain separate.

The sole production caller constructs its reqwest client with a 30-second whole-request deadline (10-second connect deadline), which applies through response chunk consumption; the existing real TCP timeout proof verifies this transport cause. Each chunk is checked before allocation against MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES; the function does not reset the request deadline or create a new retry budget.

Pure finite traversal of a materialized workflow line list. Both nested loops increment index on every traversed line and test index < len(lines); no subprocess, I/O wait or sleep occurs inside these parsing loops.

Pure fragment encoding of an immutable finite UTF-8 JSON token, not polling or an external wait. offset starts at zero and advances by min(available - len(pending), len(raw) - offset); pending is strictly below available on entry, and a full fragment yields then clears pending before the next iteration. Nonpositive available fails closed. allocation derives the actual 2 MiB per-record envelope including ordinal; no total snapshot byte/time cap is implied. The real large FleetSnapshot roundtrip checks every record bound and original full document, and the PostgreSQL slow-ASGI proof checks SQL release and threadpool encoding. Each emitted fragment yields to the transport; this classification does not claim CPU preemption or physical-worker coverage.

Only the inspection-test Gate cleanup joins its exact owned std::thread::JoinHandle after observing that same handle is_finished. The shared absolute cleanup deadline bounds prior completion polling; unfinished workers are not joined and their fixture is retained. Task abortion and semaphore return are separately checked before cleanup may claim completion. This is a completed-thread reap, not an external wait or evidence that an unresolved native effect ended.

The actual separate writer owns a cloned fixture path and reports its result over recv_timeout using one unchanged absolute 30-second budget. Its exact JoinHandle is joined only after that same handle is_finished; deadline/error paths retain the fixture rather than removing files under an unresolved writer. The isolated parent has the same total elapsed budget, reserves its last second for exact-child kill/try_wait reaping, and reports an unreaped child as failure. No scoped-thread implicit join or unconditional child wait remains; all unsafe-intermediate and atomic publication assertions remain.

Process-lifetime supervisor of the one `journalctl -k -f` follower that feeds the host memory guard; the guard itself never waits on it, it only try_sends into a capacity-1 channel. Each iteration spawns or reaps exactly one child: a previous follower is killed and reaped under a 1-second wait_timeout, a failed spawn or EOF sleeps 2 seconds before retry, and each journal line is read through take(4096) so no record grows unboundedly. The loop ends only when the helper process exits, by design, because losing the kernel signal would silently disable the guard.

Two process-lifetime guard threads, each a fixed-cadence sampler rather than an external wait: every iteration performs one bounded step (a /proc read, or a docker inventory/stop through the helper's timeout-bounded CommandRunner), receives with recv_timeout of one sample interval, and sleeps SAMPLE_INTERVAL (250 ms) so there is no hot retry. Pending stops are a BTreeMap bounded by the managed-container inventory and are dropped when a successful enumeration shows the container gone. The loops end only with the helper process, by design: a guard that exits would silently disable host protection.
Progress observation is owned by the byte-bounded image upload with its one-hour HTTP deadline; sender closure drains the snapshot and a heartbeat-sized join timeout aborts the reporter.
Progress observation is owned by the bounded object transfer and three-attempt retry; sender closure drains the snapshot and a heartbeat-sized join timeout aborts the reporter.

The runtime inspection future is selected against wait_ready_until and cancellation; the readiness owner enforces the immutable start deadline or current lease deadline and drops the observer at completion.
